manifest.json:description.text: Drag to aim, release to fire and match 3 bubbles to pop them — a cluster goes off one bubble at a time, each scoring on its own. Swap the loaded bubble for the next one whenever you like. Rainbows are jokers: one in the wall takes the colour of whatever lands on it, one fired into the rot gives a pocket of blighted bubbles their colour back — and those bubbles stay on the board. manifest.json:description.text: Coloured glass and banks of switches over a lake of lava. The ball breaks every pane of glass and flies straight past the dark buttons — until you tap: then they light up and turn solid, and the ball bounces off them and can never break them. Tap while the ball is inside a pocket of glass and it is shut in with it, runs faster and eats the whole room; tap again to let it out, or the game opens an empty pocket for you. Thirty boards across five biomes, each with its own bonus bricks: row and column blasts, bombs and multiball, the big ball, the fireball that burns through the glass and the magnet that pulls it in — and each biome brings its own living glass too: warp panes that jump every three seconds, split panes that burst into new glass, a seed that grows glass around it and electric panes behind a shield that comes and goes. Each biome teaches it in six stages — one colour, then all five and what each pays, its power, its living glass, the mix and a finale — and the stars are the wall's, not the score's: three fifths of it, nine tenths, and three for a clear within the level's par of balls. The dotted sight solves five bounces ahead.

manifest.json:description.text: An electric labyrinth is powered up for two seconds — the only look you ever get at it. Then everything goes out: the maze, the six mouths along its floor, even the walls of the arena. Fire pulses up into a mouth and the board exists only where one just hit it, arcing white and dying out over a couple of seconds, so you are echolocating a maze you can no longer see. Each mouth is a one-way flap — a pulse pushes through and it drops shut behind — and of the six, one leads to the gate at the top and five are dead ends.

manifest.json:description.text: Gelatile is a merge puzzle on a 4x4 board of jelly tiles. Swipe to slide every tile one way: two twins that meet stamp into their sum, and from 128 up a tile turns gold, then rainbow. Each of the thirty levels asks for one tile, from 128 to 2048, starting from a board already laid out in a corner, with a par of moves for the second star and a bonus for the third. Fourteen powers join the board one at a time across five biomes - a bubble bath, a jungle lodge, a crystal cave, rice terraces and a coconut beach. Tile powers freeze, petrify, ghost or hide a tile for five moves. Targets mark cells of the grid and strike after your next move, so you choose which tile lands there. And a side of the board can turn into a portal or lock shut.

manifest.json:description.text: Holepocalypse is golf against a zombie horde. The dead shamble down the fairway toward your tee, and you stand them off with a bag of five golf balls. Start your touch in the blue band around the tee to roll a ball up the grass — it ricochets off the fences and knocks zombies into each other like billiard balls, chaining knockouts — or in the orange band to lob it over the horde and drop it on their heads. Every ball that comes to rest goes back into the bag on its own. The hole hides among them: roll a ball in slowly enough and it fires a toxic shockwave that wipes most of the field — or aim for a coloured flag instead, which wins back a lost flag and loads special balls: explosive, multiball, piercing, homing, fire, ice and more. Every knockout charges two supers, from a rain of balls to a golf cart charging up the busiest lane. Thirty levels across five courses — a country club, desert links, a bayou, frozen links and a graveyard green — bring bunkers, whirlpools that swallow a zombie you knock back into them, ice where the pile-ups slide, graves the dead rise from, seven kinds of zombie and five bosses, from the Greenkeeper on his mower to the Zombie King driving skull balls back at your tee.

manifest.json:description.text: A marshmallow hangs over a lava lake, stuck to the only thing keeping it up: a falling rock. A tap flings it along the line to your finger at one fixed speed — no drag, no charge — and it sticks to the first thing it touches, then rides that rock down. Rocks melt when they reach the lava, so a landing is never a rest: the only way to stay alive is to keep climbing the ones still falling. Land high and the score pays more, chain fresh rocks and the multiplier grows. Fireballs can be grabbed too, but they only lend their back for a beat before shrugging the body off — one shade browner if you stayed. Holding the finger slows the world, but only while the focus meter under it lasts: it drains as you deliberate and the slow motion fades with it, so a long aim buys less time and a shorter preview. It stays locked for a beat once you let go before it starts filling again, and landing on a fresh rock hands part of it straight back. The lava rises the whole run, and it is the only clock. The toast is the life — white, golden, toasted, charred — and a hit on a charred marshmallow ends the run: staying on a fireball until it throws you off, or the serpent's bite. The lava is three hits at once, so only a white marshmallow comes out of it, charred. On the web the climb runs through five biomes of six levels, each bringing one thing that changes the read: the caldera and its fireballs, frozen sulphur whose ice throws the body straight up, geysers whose steam lifts whatever it touches, fault lines of rocks that split into pieces, fall to dust or blow two seconds after a landing, and the core, where the lava surges and drips. Further up the climb, giant lava bubbles carry the body up before they pop, cold water sets crusts on the lake and puts fires out, magnet crystals bend a jump, a lava serpent leaps out of a swirl, and s'mores drift down: a biscuit and a chocolate give a life back, a whole super s'more gives them all back.

manifest.json:description.text: Pawko is a pachinko board with a hand of cards over it, built for combinations. A game is five waves of balls, and before each one you drag one card of your hand onto the board: where you let it go is where the wave falls from, and the slot is dealt a new card for the next wave. Every point a peg or an exit pays is multiplied by the global multiplier in force, and fifty cards of four kinds feed it. Peg cards turn the board into fire, ice, bumpers, magnets, bombs, prisms, sparks, glass, portals or spikes for the rest of the game. Wave cards fatten, freeze, burn, charge or double one wave. Charms stay for the game and grow, from a pyromaniac to a domino of bombs. Two tricks copy or bring back the last card played. Find the right synergy and the multiplier runs away with the score. Thirty levels, four new cards a level up to the twelfth, each asking for a higher score off a board that always opens plain brass.

manifest.json:description.text: Three plates turn on one hub — teeth on the outer one — each carrying twelve coloured beads in its housings, over the twelve rays drawn between the hub and the rim. Drag a plate and it turns alone; the other two hold. Rays that would pay light up under the beads while you turn, so a plate is never moved blind, and the dial only cashes them once it comes to rest. A paid ray is re-fed from outside the rim, and the beads that fly in can land on a ray of their own, so one move can keep paying long after you let go. Every four rays the hub's meter buys a special bead, and a move that pays two rays at once — or a chain at x8 — buys a bigger one. There are eight of them and no level ever carries the whole catalogue: a Charge unzips the plate it sits on, a Nova is wild and takes its colour off the entire dial, a Bomb clears the board outright, a Fire takes the two rays either side, a Laser fires through the hub and out the far side, a Score bead arms an x2, x5 or x10 window, a Slow bead holds the eclipse back — and an Ice bead, the one you do not want, freezes the plate it breaks on. The thirty levels introduce them one at a time and run in five worlds, each with its own material for the beads and its own palette for the machine.

manifest.json:description.text: Your top spins in a battle dish and loses spin every second. Rival tops charge in: tap on the impact to fire a shockwave that marks their shell, launches them into the electric walls and winds your spin back up. Their colour is how they move and what they are immune to — blue stops, charges and dashes and shrugs off the fence, yellow saws its way in and shrugs off the crowd, red flies one straight line and blows up on whatever it touches, black circles you and hands shell points back to the others, and purple splits in two when it breaks. Thirty levels across five dishes, each with its own fence colour, its own roster and its own stretch of the track, and a ten-point boss that nothing but a perfect tap can mark. The top's colour is the only gauge — the run ends when it blows apart.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.1.lore.fr.text: Mae a appris à disparaître dans la foule d'un marché en volant des pommes. Aujourd'hui, elle vole des plans de bataille, mais laisse toujours un trognon de pomme à leur place.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.13.lore.fr.text: Justin emporte un double de tout, au cas où. Son sac pèse plus lourd que lui. Il a sauvé le régiment onze fois.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.14.lore.fr.text: Kay entend un piège enterré faire tic-tac à vingt pas. Elle le désamorce, garde la poudre et s'en sert pour allumer les bougies d'anniversaire du régiment.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.15.lore.fr.text: Sol a désamorcé trois cents pièges et en a fabriqué quatre cents, pour s'entraîner. Il parle à chaque mèche qu'il coupe. Aucune ne lui a encore répondu.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.16.lore.fr.text: Quand Mina traverse un champ de mines en fredonnant, les mines se tiennent tranquilles. Les ingénieurs jurent que ça ne marche pas comme ça. Mina jure que si.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.2.lore.fr.text: Un maître du déguisement qui possède quarante fausses moustaches et une vraie. Personne ne sait jamais laquelle, pas même Otto.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.20.lore.fr.text: Hal a passé une nuit entière à surveiller un épouvantail en attendant qu'il bouge le premier. À l'aube, il l'a coupé en deux, par principe.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.21.lore.fr.text: Frank Lee dit exactement ce qu'il pense. Et ce qu'il pense, c'est « Chargez ! ». Il est si franc qu'aucun leurre ne l'a jamais trompé.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.23.lore.fr.text: Sergent depuis cinquante ans, il est fier de n'avoir jamais été promu. Stan Firm a abattu plus d'épouvantails qu'il n'y a de champs dans le royaume.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.26.lore.fr.text: Holly abat une palissade en trois coups et la reconstruit en quatre. Elle appelle ça redécorer le camp ennemi.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.33.lore.fr.text: Rocco passe à travers les rochers, pas autour. L'intendant a renoncé à lui commander des pioches neuves. Désormais, il lui commande des rochers neufs, pour l'entraînement.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.34.lore.fr.text: Flint Eastwood prononce quatre mots par jour et n'en gaspille aucun. Les rochers entendent « Bougez ! » et, allez savoir comment, ils bougent.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.35.lore.fr.text: La capitaine Gran Knight savait déjà briser des montagnes quand la guerre n'avait pas encore de nom. Elle est petite, elle est très vieille, mais aucun rocher du royaume n'ose lui barrer la route.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.36.lore.fr.text: Wayne tient sa carte à l'envers et trouve quand même son chemin. Personne n'a jamais compris comment. Wayne non plus.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.39.lore.fr.text: Le major Hector Vane ne s'est jamais perdu, même s'il a égaré un régiment le temps d'un week-end. On l'a retrouvé exactement là où il l'avait laissé.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.43.lore.fr.text: On a mis Val Ore au défi de passer une nuit dans la crypte hantée. Elle en est sortie à l'aube avec le chapeau d'un fantôme.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.44.lore.fr.text: Le colonel Duke Upps règle chaque dispute d'un seul coup de poing, puis s'excuse poliment. Crânes, ossements et malédictions ne l'effraient pas, mais la paperasse, si.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.48.lore.fr.text: Constance a prêté serment sur un livre à cadenas, puis en a perdu la clé. Depuis, elle tient toutes ses promesses, par précaution.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.49.lore.fr.text: Keith garde les ordres secrets de l'armée dans un livre enchaîné à son poignet. Il dort avec, mange avec. Il a même traversé une rivière à la nage avec.

manifest.json:web.army.cast.7.lore.fr.text: Son seul travail : crier son propre nom. Il a fallu une semaine à l'armée pour comprendre que « Luke Out ! » voulait dire « Attention ! ».

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.0.tex.text: Pour la dernière saucisse, évidemment. {c} en ressort avec un œil au beurre noir et un lit à l'infirmerie.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.1.tex.text: Quelqu'un s'est glissé sous la tente de commandement et a filé avec un ticket. Le garde jure n'avoir rien vu.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.22.te.text: En creusant de nouvelles latrines, les sapeurs sont tombés sur un vieux coffre rempli de pièces.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.29.te.text: Le camp a vendu des bottes en trop et de vieux casques à très bon prix.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.32.te.text: Les enfants du village sont venus voir les soldats et ont donné un sticker pour la collection.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.34.te.text: L'odeur de la cuisine a attiré du monde. De nouvelles têtes attendent à la tente de recrutement.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.38.te.text: Le potager du camp a donné plus que ce qu'il fallait. Le surplus s'est vendu contre deux tickets.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.4.tex.text: La moitié du camp a passé la nuit à gémir. Les cas les plus graves sont à l'infirmerie.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.5.tex.text: Une lanterne s'est renversée entre les sacs de la réserve. Le feu est éteint, mais il faut racheter ce qui a été brûlé.

manifest.json:web.army.events.list.8.tit.text: La tente abattue par la tempête

manifest.json:web.army.missions.list.48..text: Chaque automne, les gobelins tiennent la foire de la Crasse sous la montagne, où tout se vend, y compris des tickets rares et la solde du camp rouge. Les mises sont hautes et les dés pipés. Envoie une escouade aux poches profondes et aux nerfs solides.

En fantôme, tu traverses les mines, les pièges, les lasers, les comètes et les cordes électrifiées.

manifest.json:web.copy.fr.strings.Neithe.text: Ni l'armure du bouclier ni l'état de fantôme ne te protégeront d'une chute dans un trou.

manifest.json:web.copy.fr.strings.Ride a.text: Suis une figure comme une boucle jusqu'à la fin pour obtenir une récompense de point.

manifest.json:web.copy.fr.strings.Sparks.text: Des étincelles parcourent toujours une corde avant que l'électricité ne frappe.

manifest.json:copy.fr.tagline.text: Glissez-vous dans la peau de Vipera et explorez cinq biomes remplis de pièges et de défis. Un simple Tap suffit pour changer de direction mais il faudra maîtriser l'art de l'ondulation pour faire le plein de bonus et devenir le roi du classement !

manifest.json:description.text: A viper races up an endless burrow. Every tap flips the side it carves toward, so a rhythm of taps weaves it through the thorns. Gems grow the body — and the longer it gets, the higher its head rides and the less time there is to read what comes next. Eat all the way to full length and the scales plate over: the armour eats the next bite for free. Unarmoured, a thorn strips the body back to a stump and costs one of only three lives — the whole ladder has to be eaten again, at the speed the run has already reached.
